prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: Daggerfall Unity native pixel-art NPC eye animation atlas
Input images: Image 1 is the exact source upper-face reference atlas; preserve its character identity, pixel clusters, framing, palette and pixel-art style.
Primary request: Create one complete 2-by-2 atlas with four exact, equal cells, overall wide canvas aspect ratio 64:35. Each cell is the same 64x35 native upper-face crop. Order: top-left LEFT gaze open, top-right RIGHT gaze open, bottom-left LEFT gaze half-closed, bottom-right RIGHT gaze half-closed.
Subject: The source character's face, brows, small eyes, hair and surrounding pixels.
Style/medium: Faithful low-resolution pixel art with compact stepped pixel clusters; no smoothing or vector shapes.
Composition/framing: Keep the source crop and framing identical in all four cells. Do not add separators, labels, margins, borders or transparency. Upper row keeps the source's open neutral lids. Lower row uses the source's narrow half-closed eye aperture, with upper lids lowered and lower lids, cheeks and brows anchored.
Constraints: Preserve the exact narrow source aperture and brow shape. Keep each iris compact, dark olive-brown with a subtle muted amber tone and only a tiny warm glint; preserve the source's shaded brown-gray eye whites without making them pale cream or bright horizontal bands. Move both colored iris and pupil clusters together by about one native pixel toward the same canvas side for each gaze, with natural matching convergence; do not leave either iris centered while the other moves. Left and right gaze should be clear but modest. In half-closed cells, upper lids occlude the upper part of each iris while retaining the same lateral gaze. Preserve the original identity, skin, hair, palette, pixel grid, exterior pixels, neutral expression and unchanged brow position. No vertical or diagonal gaze, no cheek movement, no iris enlargement, no widened sclera, no new glints, no reflections, no changed face details.
